messages.author: 89a72ee247eb088d
messages.subject: Error/Warning regarding Left-hand side of sampling statement (~) and rejection of Metropolis proposa
parts:
Hi, we are just starting to learn Stan and we are testing some discrete choice models estimation by Stan. Particularly, we are trying to estimate a simple mixed-nested logit model where we estimate the probability of 3 modes of transport being chosen namely, Rail, Bus, and Car.
There are two nests, the first containing only the Rail mode, and the other nest containing the Bus and Car. We induce correlation between the Bus and Car nest by introducing a random variable, eps, that only comes in on the utility equations of Bus and Car. The Stan code is as below:

mnl_code <-  "
data {
    int<lower=2> K;   //number of alternatives (three)
    int<lower=0> N;   //number of samples
    int<lower=1> D;   //number of predictors
    int<lower=0,upper=1> y[N,K];    //chosen alternative
    matrix [K,D]  x[N];    //matrix of alternatives vs predictors
  }
parameters {
    vector[D] beta;
    real<lower=0.01,upper=5> sigma;
}
model {
    vector[N] eps;
    for (n in 1:N) eps[n] ~ normal(0,sigma);
    for (n in 1:N) {
      vector[K] v; vector[K] lp;
        v <- x[n]*beta;
          lp[1] <- log( exp(v[1]        )/( exp(v[1])+exp(v[2]+eps[n])+exp(v[3]+eps[n])) );
          lp[2] <- log( exp(v[2]+eps[n] )/( exp(v[1])+exp(v[2]+eps[n])+exp(v[3]+eps[n])) );
          lp[3] <- log( exp(v[3]+eps[n] )/( exp(v[1])+exp(v[2]+eps[n])+exp(v[3]+eps[n])) );
        increment_log_prob(lp[1]*y[n,1]+lp[2]*y[n,2]+lp[3]*y[n,3]);
    }
}
"

We are getting a parser warning:

DIAGNOSTIC(S) FROM PARSER:
Warning (non-fatal):
Left-hand side of sampling statement (~) may contain a non-linear transform of a parameter or local variable.
If so, you need to call increment_log_prob() with the log absolute determinant of the Jacobian of the transform.
Left-hand-side of sampling statement:
    eps[n] ~ normal(...)


and errors:
[596] "Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected because of the following issue:"                       
[597] "Exception thrown at line 15: stan::math::normal_log: Random variable is nan, but must not be nan!"                                    
[598] "If this warning occurs sporadically, such as for highly constrained variable types like covariance matrices, then the sampler is fine,"
[599] "but if this warning occurs often then your model may be either severely ill-conditioned or misspecified."                             
[600] "Rejecting initial value:"                                                                                                             
[601] "  Error evaluating the log probability at the initial value."                                                                         
[602] "Initialization between (--2, -2) failed after 100 attempts. "                                                                         
[603] " Try specifying initial values, reducing ranges of constrained values, or reparameterizing the model."                                
[1] "error occurred during calling the sampler; sampling not done"

We really want to learn how Stan works and how to properly use it; we have also tried looking for solutions in the manual to no avail. Would really appreciate all the help we can get in our simple model.

Thanks!

messages.subject: Re: Error/Warning regarding Left-hand side of sampling statement (~) and rejection of Metropolis proposa
parts:
eps looks like an unknown parameter so you need to declare it in the parameters block. Right now you're declaring it in the model block, which will only work if it's a transformation of an existing parameter. 

Do that help get it running?

Jonah

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: Error/Warning regarding Left-hand side of sampling statement (~) and rejection of Metropolis proposa
parts:
Just to clarify, when you declare something in the model block it's going to be initialized to NA so if you don't assign a value (either a fixed value or by transforming an existing parameter) then it will still have an NA value. 

So as a simple example: 

parameters{
  real mu;
  real<lower=0> sigma;
}
model {
  real theta;
  theta ~ normal(mu, sigma);
}

won't work because theta isn't either a parameter or a fixed quantity. But if you declare theta in the parameters block or assigned it a real number as a value before using it, it would be valid. 

Something like this is also valid: 

parameters{
  real x;
  real mu;
  real<lower=0> sigma;
}
model {
  real theta;
  theta <- f(x); // for some function f
  theta ~ normal(mu, sigma)
}

but then you have a function of a parameter on the left side of a sampling statement and a Jacobian adjustment may be necessary (if the transformation f is non-linear). 

Jonah
